card_says: Pipeline company, owned by BP, SOCAR and Snam (20% each), Fluxys (19%), Enagás (16%) and Axpo (5%)
source_says: TAP's own article of 15 November 2025 lists five shareholders holding 20 percent each: bp, SOCAR, Snam, Fluxys and Enagás. Axpo is not named, and Fluxys is not at 19 percent nor Enagás at 16 percent. The card's split matches an earlier period; the holdings on the card were not current as of November 2025. The page does not say when or in what stages they changed.

source.title: TAP marks five years of safe and reliable operations

card_says: Owner of Cerro Matoso since May 2015
source_says: South32 held Cerro Matoso at the time of the case. Its Annual Report for the year to 30 June 2025 states that it entered a binding agreement on 7 July 2025 to divest the Cerro Matoso nickel operation, for nominal upfront consideration and future cash payments of up to US$100 million, with completion expected in late H1 FY26 subject to conditions.

card_says: Owner and builder when the dredging and spill happened; Gazprom took a majority in December 2006 (FoE Japan)
source_says: Oil & Gas Journal, dated 24 April 2007, reports the acquisition as done: Gazprom paid US$7.45 billion in cash under a sale and purchase agreement with Sakhalin Energy's shareholders for 50 percent plus one share, leaving Shell at about 27.5 percent, Mitsui 12.5 percent and Mitsubishi 10 percent. The article gives no signing date, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the card's December 2006 date for the agreement; it places the completion as reported in April 2007.

source.title: Gazprom acquires controlling stake in Sakhalin-2

card_says: Indian microfinance lender, which went public in August 2010
source_says: An NSE filing of June 2019 records that the company, formerly SKS Microfinance Limited and renamed Bharat Financial Inclusion Limited, had its assets and liabilities transferred to IndusInd Bank with effect from 4 July 2019 under a scheme sanctioned by the NCLT (appointed date 1 January 2018), so it ceased to exist as a separate listed lender from that date.

source.title: Press release on the merger of Bharat Financial Inclusion Limited with IndusInd Bank
source.publisher: National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) filing

card_says: Original lease holder, hq Toronto, Canada
source_says: A March 2010 company release records that Tiomin Resources Inc traded on the TSX as TIO and that shareholders voted on 15 March 2010 to rename the company Vaaldiam Mining Inc (TSX: VAA) on completing its acquisition of Vaaldiam Resources, so the name Tiomin Resources was dropped in 2010. Neither source opened states a Toronto head office, so the card's headquarters is unverified rather than contradicted.

source.title: Tiomin Resources Inc. Shareholders Approve Acquisition of Vaaldiam

card_says: Case title describes it as 'A Hong Kong-Owned Iron Ore Mine'
source_says: Petromindo, reporting on 19 September 2016, describes PT Mikgro Metal Perdana as a joint venture between PT Allindo Indonesia and China's Aempire Resource Ltd. It gives no split and does not name Hong Kong.

source.title: MEMR tells Mikgro to relocate iron ore mine in N. Sulawesi

card_says: Malaysian logging group. Oxfam links it to the Turubu lease through shared addresses, directors and shareholders and inquiry findings; the lease holder is Sepik Oil Palm Plantation Ltd
source_says: ACT NOW! reports that in May 2021 a Malaysian newspaper carried a statement from WTK Holdings Berhad that it had no logging operations in Papua New Guinea, and that the company did not reply to a request for clarification before publication. ACT NOW! itself links more than 30 PNG-registered companies to the group through common directors and shareholders, at least nine of them logging companies.

source.title: PNG's Timber Barons: #1 - The WTK Cluster

card_says: Third plant named by the government, 'Shanghai Kangshuo Co Ltd'
source_says: China Daily's February 2012 report on the Shanghai municipal government findings gives the full name as Shanghai Kangshuo Waste Recycling Co and describes it as a recycler of used goods and materials whose plant soil in the Kangqiao area of Pudong contained excessive lead and zinc, and which had since relocated.

source.title: 3 companies responsible for child lead poisoning

source_says: Philex Mining's own Integrated Annual Corporate Governance Report for 2023, filed on its website, gives the principal office as 2nd Floor, Reliance cor. Sheridan Sts., Mandaluyong City 1550. A market-data profile also gives Mandaluyong City. On the company's 2023 filing the head office was in Mandaluyong, not Pasig; the filings opened do not say when it moved, so an earlier Pasig address is not excluded.

card_says: Shareholder, named as Ratchaburi Electricity Generating Holding
source_says: The company's own background page says it was founded on 7 March 2000 under the former name Ratchaburi Electricity Generating Holding Public Company Limited and is now RATCH Group Public Company Limited, trading on the Stock Exchange of Thailand as RATCH. The page does not give the date of the name change.

card_says: Parent and operator; hq London, United Kingdom
source_says: Daily Maverick (April 2021) names the operator of the Cato Ridge mercury recovery factory as Thor SA, closed by government in 1991, after which the Thor group restructured through a demerger. The parent it names is the UK-based Tato Holdings group, 'the restructured former parent company of Thor SA', which agreed to set aside nearly R174 million for the clean-up and which says in its annual report that it sold Thor to a South African third party. No source opened names a company called 'Thor Chemical Holdings', so that name on the card is unverified; the UK location of the parent is consistent with the card.

source.title: At long last, Thor's poisonous mercury is getting cleaned up
